AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Methadone has been associated with lower overall survival (OS) in patients with chronic pain. There are no data available on the association of methadone with OS in cancer patients.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Our aim was to compare the OS in cancer outpatients undergoing opioid rotation (OR) to methadone and other strong opioids.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Demographics, symptoms, and morphine equivalent daily dose (MEDD) were collected in patients who underwent OR from strong opioids to either methadone or other strong opioids and returned for a follow-up within six weeks.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING/SUBJECTS
AbstractText.content: Nine hundred thirty-eight consecutive outpatients to the supportive care center of a tertiary cancer center were reviewed.

AbstractText.Label: MEASUREMENTS
AbstractText.content: Kaplan-Meier curves were used to evaluate survival.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Of a total of 164 eligible patients, 54/76 patients who underwent OR to methadone and 48/88 patients who underwent OR to other opioids returned for a follow-up visit. The median age was 56 years, 54% were male, and 87% had advanced cancer. There were no significant differences between the two groups in patient characteristics, performance status, MEDD, and pain scores. The Kaplan-Meier curves revealed no significant difference in median OS between all patients undergoing OR to methadone and other opioids [3.75 months (95% confidence interval, CI, 2.30-6.46) vs. 2.62 months (95% CI 1.74-4.33); p = 0.35] and also among those who returned for a follow-up following an OR to methadone and other opioids [5.15 months (95% CI 3.64-7.41) vs. 5.90 months (95% CI 2.62-9.28); p = 0.89].

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: We observed no significant difference in OS in cancer patients in methadone group compared to other opioids.
